title: Flow times minutes
hook: A flow rate is not the final volume until duration joins it.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Convert a constant flow rate and duration into volume.

misconception: Litres per minute already states total litres used.
objective: Convert a constant flow rate and duration into volume.

claims.text: Two hypothetical constant flows are 6L/min and 3L/min, each running four minutes. Scaled model; illustrative constant flows; no fixture instructions.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Minutes=4min, A=24L and B=12L. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",6,"x"]; B=["*",3,"x"]; x denotes Minutes. At x=4, A=24, B=12; recall at x=7: B=21. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: A volume per minute multiplied by minutes gives volume. Keeping duration equal isolates the flow-rate difference. Actual flow can vary, so the picture demonstrates the stated arithmetic only.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",6,"x"]; B=["*",3,"x"]; x denotes Minutes. At x=4, A=24, B=12; recall at x=7: B=21. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: Two hypothetical constant flows are 6L/min and 3L/min, each running four minutes. Change only Minutes to 7min. What is B (3L/min) now? Correct: 21L. Use B's stated rule with Minutes=7min: it gives 21L. A volume per minute multiplied by minutes gives volume. Keeping duration equal isolates the flow-rate difference. Actual flow can vary, so the picture demonstrates the stated arithmetic only.

recall.question: Two hypothetical constant flows are 6L/min and 3L/min, each running four minutes. Change only Minutes to 7min. What is B (3L/min) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Minutes=7min: it gives 21L. A volume per minute multiplied by minutes gives volume. Keeping duration equal isolates the flow-rate difference. Actual flow can vary, so the picture demonstrates the stated arithmetic only.

safety.assumptions: Two hypothetical constant flows are 6L/min and 3L/min, each running four minutes.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
